I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 cash and a fully built pink monopoly. The opponent has only $29 and a dark blue monopoly with heavily mortgaged properties. Another opponent is bankrupt, and a third is in jail with $763.

The auction is for North Carolina Avenue. The current high bid is $51 by p4. I am the only remaining bidder after p1 dropped out. My plan is to cap the bid at roughly $150 so I can mortgage the property and block p4 from completing a Pennsylvania Avenue and North Carolina Avenue pair.

I will raise the bid to $52. Pacific is mortgaged by p1, so neither player can complete a green monopoly without trading.

Blocking p4 from a second green is strategic, but the monopoly cannot be built immediately. I am standing on p4's mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue, so no rent is due this turn. I need to roll carefully, since p1's Park Place and Boardwalk could charge large rent.

I can sell all 12 pink houses for $600. Combined with my cash, I have roughly $1326 in total liquidity. Buying North Carolina Avenue for $52 leaves me with about $674. That is enough to cover the $1100 rent on Park Place if I sell houses.

Boardwalk at $1700 is fatal even with all house sales and mortgaging. I am currently on Pennsylvania Avenue, so I need to map the board to see where a roll of +2 lands.

I mapped the standard Monopoly board. I am on space 34, Pennsylvania Avenue. I am now checking where a roll of +2 lands.

A roll of 3 lands on Park Place for $1100. A roll of 5 lands on Boardwalk for $1700. Selling 9 houses covers the Park Place shortfall. Even a $200 bid leaves enough cash to survive both.

The $150 cap is a wash strategy. I will bid $52 and raise by one dollar each turn to extract value from p4, who owns Pennsylvania Avenue and wants North Carolina Avenue.
